evidence.claim: The Prime Minister heads the Cabinet and executive power is exercised by or under the authority of the Prime Minister; the President appoints the MP who commands a parliamentary majority.
evidence.title: The Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, Bangladesh
evidence.publication_date: n.d. consolidated text in force in 2022
evidence.excerpt: The Prime Minister heads the Cabinet and executive power is exercised by or under the authority of the Prime Minister; the President appoints the MP who commands a parliamentary majority.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary constitutional text from the official legal repository.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to Sheikh Hasina's office and formal authority, but not to any specific 2022 nuclear-risk decision.
contrary_evidence: Formal executive authority does not prove responsible use of that authority in any specific year.

evidence.claim: Abdur Rouf Talukder joined as the 12th governor of Bangladesh Bank on 12 July 2022 after a long finance-ministry career; the bio says he contributed to budget reform, macroeconomic management, and IT in public financial management.
evidence.title: Mr. Abdur Rouf Talukder Former Governor, Bangladesh Bank
evidence.excerpt: Abdur Rouf Talukder joined as the 12th governor of Bangladesh Bank on 12 July 2022 after a long finance-ministry career; the bio says he contributed to budget reform, macroeconomic management, and IT in public financial management.
evidence.source_locator: bio paragraphs identifying his appointment and prior roles
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary official biography page from the central bank, with direct appointment and career details.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect. The page does not show Sheikh Hasina ordering the appointment, but it documents the government-selected central-bank leadership available to her administration.
contrary_evidence: The same bio shows a senior finance-ministry insider, so it supports competence but also suggests closeness to the executive rather than institutional independence.

evidence.claim: The IMF said Bangladesh entered the pandemic with macroeconomic stability, announced support packages worth Tk 1.9 trillion by curtailing non-priority spending, and had macro policies that kept inflation stable, debt-to-GDP low, and external buffers adequate.
evidence.title: IMF Executive Board Concludes 2021 Article IV Consultation with Bangladesh
evidence.excerpt: The IMF said Bangladesh entered the pandemic with macroeconomic stability, announced support packages worth Tk 1.9 trillion by curtailing non-priority spending, and had macro policies that kept inflation stable, debt-to-GDP low, and external buffers adequate.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official IMF country assessment with concrete macro indicators and policy response description.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the Hasina administration's economic policy, not to Hasina personally; the source evaluates government and central-bank actions.
contrary_evidence: The same report warns that FY22 inflation would rise to 5.9 percent and the current account deficit would widen, so it is not an unalloyed success story.

evidence.claim: IMF directors urged Bangladesh to monitor inflation closely, normalize monetary policy, gradually increase exchange-rate flexibility, safeguard reserves, strengthen bank regulation and supervision, improve corporate governance, and address corruption.
evidence.title: IMF Executive Board Concludes 2021 Article IV Consultation with Bangladesh
evidence.excerpt: IMF directors urged Bangladesh to monitor inflation closely, normalize monetary policy, gradually increase exchange-rate flexibility, safeguard reserves, strengthen bank regulation and supervision, improve corporate governance, and address corruption.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official IMF Board summary with explicit reform prescriptions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect. It reflects the policy environment and the government's available choices rather than a direct personal act by Hasina.
contrary_evidence: The report also acknowledges the government's rapid pandemic response and fiscal prudence, so the record is mixed rather than purely negative.

evidence.claim: The IMF said the new program aimed to restore macroeconomic stability, protect the vulnerable, create fiscal space, contain inflation, modernize the monetary policy framework, strengthen the financial sector, improve the business climate, and build climate resilience.
evidence.title: IMF Staff Reaches Staff-Level Agreement with Bangladesh on the Extended Credit Facility/Extended Fund Facility and the Resilience and Sustainability Facility
evidence.excerpt: The IMF said the new program aimed to restore macroeconomic stability, protect the vulnerable, create fiscal space, contain inflation, modernize the monetary policy framework, strengthen the financial sector, improve the business climate, and build climate resilience.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary IMF mission statement with detailed policy objectives and rationale.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect, as a government-level reform program negotiated with the Hasina administration rather than a personal statement by Hasina.
contrary_evidence: The same press release says the economy had been hit by a sharp widening of the current account deficit, rapid reserve decline, rising inflation, and slowing growth.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said its $250 million financing would help Bangladesh build a stronger fiscal and financial sector, streamline the bank recovery framework, and support a legislative framework on payments to create a more efficient financial system.
evidence.title: World Bank Helps Bangladesh Build Economic Resilience
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said its $250 million financing would help Bangladesh build a stronger fiscal and financial sector, streamline the bank recovery framework, and support a legislative framework on payments to create a more efficient financial system.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary World Bank press release on a Bangladesh policy credit with specific reform content.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government-level policy action under the Hasina administration; the source does not isolate personal direction by Hasina.
contrary_evidence: The financing was designed to address resilience gaps, which implies the existing fiscal and financial systems still needed strengthening.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said Bangladesh needed a strong reform agenda to sustain growth, especially to address trade competitiveness erosion, financial-sector vulnerabilities, orderly urbanization, digital development, climate change, private-sector financing, and export diversification.
evidence.title: Strong Trade Competitiveness, Financial Sector, and Well-functioning Cities are Critical for Sustained Growth in Bangladesh: World Bank
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said Bangladesh needed a strong reform agenda to sustain growth, especially to address trade competitiveness erosion, financial-sector vulnerabilities, orderly urbanization, digital development, climate change, private-sector financing, and export diversification.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary World Bank country press release summarizing a country economic memorandum.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is a country-level reform assessment under the Hasina administration, not a direct ruler statement.
contrary_evidence: The same piece credits Bangladesh with remarkable development progress and very fast growth over the previous decade.

evidence.claim: The e-GP portal brought public procurement online, cut procurement costs by about 7 percent, reduced tender time from 100 days to 57 days, processed 80 percent of public procurement expenditure in FY21, and improved integrity by reducing external influences and preserving audit trails.
evidence.title: World Bank-Funded Project Drives Public Procurement Reform in Bangladesh
evidence.excerpt: The e-GP portal brought public procurement online, cut procurement costs by about 7 percent, reduced tender time from 100 days to 57 days, processed 80 percent of public procurement expenditure in FY21, and improved integrity by reducing external influences and preserving audit trails.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: World Bank results page with concrete implementation and outcome metrics.
evidence.period_fit: retrospective but highly relevant to 2022 governance conditions
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government-level reform implementation under the Hasina administration; the result page does not prove personal oversight by Hasina.
contrary_evidence: The need to strengthen procurement integrity implies prior corruption and influence risks were material.

evidence.claim: The FY2022-23 budget speech made inflation control, a competitive exchange rate, continued economic development, employment generation, and emergency support for low-income people explicit priorities, including a Tk 5,000 crore fund for shocks from natural disasters or other crises.
evidence.title: National Budget Speech 2022-2023
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Finance, Government of Bangladesh
evidence.excerpt: The FY2022-23 budget speech made inflation control, a competitive exchange rate, continued economic development, employment generation, and emergency support for low-income people explicit priorities, including a Tk 5,000 crore fund for shocks from natural disasters or other crises.
evidence.source_locator: Chapter Seven and the low-income support section, lines 894-901 and 1237-1242
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary government budget speech with explicit policy priorities and allocations.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect. The document is the finance minister's budget speech for the Hasina government; it reflects administration priorities, not a direct personal statement by Hasina.
contrary_evidence: The speech is aspirational and does not itself prove successful execution.

evidence.claim: The budget allocated Tk 183,425 crore to social infrastructure, Tk 31,761 crore to primary and mass education, Tk 29,282 crore to health, Tk 44,690 crore to local government and rural development, and Tk 4,290 crore to women and children affairs; it also said social safety-net coverage had reached 29 percent of households and allocations had risen almost eight-fold since FY2008-09.
evidence.title: National Budget Speech 2022-2023
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Finance, Government of Bangladesh
evidence.excerpt: The budget allocated Tk 183,425 crore to social infrastructure, Tk 31,761 crore to primary and mass education, Tk 29,282 crore to health, Tk 44,690 crore to local government and rural development, and Tk 4,290 crore to women and children affairs; it also said social safety-net coverage had reached 29 percent of households and allocations had risen almost eight-fold since FY2008-09.
evidence.source_locator: Chapter Six and social-safety-net section, lines 1028-1033, 1799-1801, 5651-5654, 2403-2406, and 2515-2519
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary budget text with explicit sectoral allocations and social-protection targets.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect government policy under the Hasina administration; the speech itself is by the finance minister, not Hasina personally.
contrary_evidence: The speech reports planned rather than audited outcomes, so implementation remains to be verified.

evidence.claim: TIB said Bangladesh scored 25 on the CPI 2022, ranked 147th, and that the lack of visible action over the previous decade and the growth of impunity and political influence over accountability institutions had worsened corruption control.
evidence.title: CPI 2022: Disappointing global and Bangladesh performances
evidence.excerpt: TIB said Bangladesh scored 25 on the CPI 2022, ranked 147th, and that the lack of visible action over the previous decade and the growth of impunity and political influence over accountability institutions had worsened corruption control.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: National TI chapter summarizing the CPI results and providing Bangladesh-specific interpretation with concrete score/rank data.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Country-level anti-corruption performance under the Hasina administration; the report does not isolate individual personal decisions.
contrary_evidence: TIB explicitly notes the government's repeated anti-corruption pledges, so the source mixes stated intent with poor implementation.

evidence.claim: The HIES 2022 report found that families spent about 42 percent of monthly income on food and only Tk 923 on average was left as savings, indicating substantial household budget pressure.
evidence.title: Household Expenditure Survey 2022: Families Spend 42% of Income on Food | BBS Report
evidence.excerpt: The HIES 2022 report found that families spent about 42 percent of monthly income on food and only Tk 923 on average was left as savings, indicating substantial household budget pressure.
evidence.source_locator: Sector-wise expenditure section and the opening paragraphs, lines 41-46 and 53-55
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reputable local reporting of the official BBS survey, but the underlying survey report is more authoritative than the news article.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Country-level outcome under the Hasina administration; not direct proof of ruler action or omission.
contrary_evidence: The survey is a 2022 snapshot and does not by itself separate government policy from imported inflation or private consumption shocks.

evidence.claim: The provisional Labour Force Survey 2022 said Bangladesh's total labour force reached 73.41 million and the unemployment rate fell to 3.6 percent from 4.2 percent in 2016-17.
evidence.title: Total labour force in the country is 73.41m
evidence.excerpt: The provisional Labour Force Survey 2022 said Bangladesh's total labour force reached 73.41 million and the unemployment rate fell to 3.6 percent from 4.2 percent in 2016-17.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official news service reporting BBS provisional survey results; useful for labor-market context but still one-step removed from the underlying report.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Country-level outcome under the administration, not direct evidence of a specific Hasina policy choice.
contrary_evidence: The piece reports labor-force expansion more than job quality, so it does not settle underemployment or real-wage questions.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Bangladesh's current account deficit widened to 4.2 percent of GDP in FY22, foreign-exchange reserves fell below $40 billion, and the government sought IMF support after import costs surged and remittances fell.
evidence.title: Bangladesh’s current account deficit widens as imports surge
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Bangladesh's current account deficit widened to 4.2 percent of GDP in FY22, foreign-exchange reserves fell below $40 billion, and the government sought IMF support after import costs surged and remittances fell.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting replicated by a major Bangladeshi outlet with concrete macro figures.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This reflects the Hasina government's macroeconomic position and response, not necessarily a personally directed policy error.
contrary_evidence: The article also notes Bangladesh had been one of the world's fastest-growing economies for years, so the 2022 deterioration sits against a strong prior trend.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said extreme poverty in Bangladesh had fallen to 5 percent in 2022 from 9 percent in 2016, with other wellbeing indicators such as infant mortality, stunting, electricity access, sanitation, and education also improving.
evidence.title: Structural Reforms are Essential to Sustain Growth & Poverty Reduction in Bangladesh
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said extreme poverty in Bangladesh had fallen to 5 percent in 2022 from 9 percent in 2016, with other wellbeing indicators such as infant mortality, stunting, electricity access, sanitation, and education also improving.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary World Bank feature summarizing 2022 poverty survey results and broader welfare trends.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Outcome-level evidence under the Hasina administration, not direct proof of a specific policy choice.
contrary_evidence: The same feature warns that growth sustainability now requires policy adjustments because of balance-of-payments pressure, rising inflation, and financial-sector vulnerabilities.
